title: Goose Boss Animation
eyebrow: Design for approval · The Honking Deep (the goose boss) · nothing built yet

short.lead: You asked for the goose boss (art/goose, The Honking Deep) to be animated as a Soulslike boss with five attacks and a phase transition. Today the goose is one finished mesh with no skeleton and no animation, so this needs a rig (a skeleton bound to the mesh) first, then the clips (the animations). The four choices below decide which five attacks it has, what the phase transition looks like, which extra clips come with them, and where the result goes.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: The pass 19 goose: one mesh of 272,380 triangles, three baked 4096 px textures, exported as goose.glb, goose.fbx and goose.blend, 6.75 m tall. Its stats.json records 0 bones. There is no rig or clip code anywhere in the models repo. The art-pipeline plugin ships only render_views.py and review_sheet.py, and this work reuses both for every review. The mesh itself is not changed unless you pick the new-geometry phase transition.

items: Which five attacks, which phase transition, which extra clips, and where the finished clips go.
Pick an option for each of the four questions under Choices, or write your own.

A generic (non-humanoid) skeleton of 59 bones: root, pelvis, three spine and two tail bones; the main neck with 7 bones, a head and a jaw; each side neck with 6 bones, a head and a jaw; one bone for each dead maple crown, so the crowns can sway and grow; each wing with a shoulder, upper arm, forearm, hand and four bare finger bones; each leg with thigh, shin, tarsus and toes. A script builds it and binds it to the mesh with automatic weights (Blender works out how far each bone pulls on the nearby surface). Extra rules keep the teeth, ribs and finger bones rigid.

Each clip is keyframed by a script from named poses, with a wind-up, a strike and a recovery so every attack can be read and dodged, which is what makes it feel Soulslike. Every clip stays in place (the goose does not travel across the ground; the game moves it) and carries hit events, which are marked moments in the clip when damage can land.
The rig gets a posed review sheet before any clip is made. Each clip gets 8 stills on the real goose and an MP4, and I write down what I saw before the next clip starts.
Nothing from you. Every sheet will be in the pull request for you to see.
Everything is committed on AjsAgent/import-models and reaches main only by a pull request, as you asked.
You check the clips, then merge.

changes: new
art/goose/build_rig.py
Builds the 59-bone skeleton and binds it to the goose mesh.

Takes the bone positions from the design numbers already in spec.json (neck curves, wing joints, leg joints), so the rig will follow the mesh if the mesh is ever rebuilt. Writes goose_rigged.blend and a posed review sheet.
new
art/goose/goose_clips.py
The named poses and the clips built from them.

One pose library (rest, crouch, rear-up, wings spread and so on) and one function per clip. Each function times its poses with easing (smooth starts and stops), anticipation (a small wind-up before a move) and overshoot (going slightly past the target, then settling back). Exports goose_anims.fbx (animation only) and a clip manifest, which lists each clip's length, whether it loops, and its hit events.
new
art/goose/clips/
Review stills and an MP4 per clip.
8 stills per clip on the real model plus a short MP4, so each clip can be judged without Blender.
chg
art/goose/spec.json and README.md
Gain a rig section and a clip list.
0 bones, no clips
59 bones, the chosen clips with timings
The README's known-gaps line, which says there is no rig and no clips, is updated to say what now exists.
keep
The goose mesh and textures
Unchanged, unless you pick the new-geometry phase transition.
goose.glb, goose.fbx and the textures stay exactly as pass 19.
choices: Built on what only this goose has. 1. Triple Peck: the three heads strike one after another, the last one held back to catch an early dodge. 2. Wing Rake: a wide sweep of the bone-fingered wing. 3. Rearing Stomp: it rears up flapping and slams both feet down. 4. Neck Lunge Grab: the main neck shoots forward, seizes, shakes and throws. 5. Death Honk: all three heads scream in a close-range blast.

Built on goose movement. 1. Hesitation Peck: a long held wind-up, then a fast peck. 2. Flapping Charge: a running charge with wings beating. 3. Leap and Dive: it jumps and dive-bombs the spot. 4. Wing Gust: a flap that pushes the player away. 5. Turning Tail Sweep: it spins and sweeps with its tail and rear.
Name any five attacks from the lists above, or suggest your own.

Option A uses the three heads and the finger-bone wings, the two things that set this boss apart from a large bird. It still covers the usual Soulslike attack types: a delayed attack, a sweep, an area slam, a grab and a burst.
What happens at the phase transition?

It staggers to its knees, the side heads hang limp, then the main head snaps upright, the dead maple crowns grow by half, the wings unfold to full span and all three heads scream. This works by scaling bones, so it needs no new geometry.
The maple-leaf brand on the breast splits into a fourth maw full of teeth. Needs a new pass on the model, with its own review, before any animation starts. That makes it the bigger job.
Option A reads clearly as a second phase and leaves the approved pass 19 model untouched. Option B is the more dramatic reveal, but it reopens the model you have already signed off.
Which clips come beyond the five attacks and the transition?
Adds idle, walk, turn on the spot, stagger (hit reaction) and death. Five more clips.
The five attacks and the phase transition, nothing else.
The playable set plus phase-two idle
Everything in option A, plus a more agitated idle for phase two. That makes six extra clips.

A boss with attacks but no idle, walk or death clip cannot be dropped into a fight, so I suggest the five supporting clips in option A. You only asked for the attacks and the transition, so option B is the strict reading of your request.
Where does the finished work go?
The rigged .blend file, the animation FBX, the clip manifest and all review stills and MP4s, committed in Ajw2003/models.
Also import it into a Unity project (tell me which one). Unity cannot run in this cloud session, so that part would be untested. I would hand it to you with the exact menu item to run.
Nothing in PlunderSpell or the other repos mentions the goose today, so I don't know which game it belongs to. Option A keeps this repo self-contained.
